title: Midwatch timelines and sweeps
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal midwatch cheat-sheet — timeline template + sweeps + temporary ops play fragments. Not polished, meant for rapid handoffs and quick mental model while covering the 00:00–06:00 window.

TL;DR:
- Do a full surface sweep at start of shift (see 'start sweep' below).
- Then run light sweeps every 30m and health-checks every hour.
- If latency or error spike: failover to tier-b fallback, open JIRA, ping oncall-sre.

Start sweep (first 10m):
- Check global alert dashboard (Grafana: Ops > Global Overview). Note any alerts and their severity.
- Confirm primary region (us-west-2) has no queued deployment spikes.
- kubectl top nodes, pods on inference namespace: kubectl -n inference get pods -o wide | grep -E "(CrashLoopBackOff|Pending)"
- Journal tail for redwood-agent and runtime: sudo journalctl -u redwood-agent -f --since "5m" (scan for OOMs/segfaults)
- Quick eviction check: prometheus query: sum(rate(container_memory_working_set_bytes[5m])) by (node) > node_memory_bytes? (copy from dashboard)
- Check DedSec (dedicated) queue length: curl -s "https://internal-api.redwood/dedicated/queue" | jq '.pending'

Recurring light sweep (every 30m):
- Check error rate trend for the last 30m (Grafana panel).
- Verify KV cache hit ratio > 85% for hot routes (embedding and chat).
- Check autoscaler logs: grep "scale" /var/log/autoscaler.log | tail -n 50
- Headcount note: if sustained error > threshold for 15m, escalate.

Hourly health-check (every hour on the :10):
- Run synthetic sample request (use local curl script /usr/local/bin/synthetic-check). Expect 95th latency < 600ms for text-gen-default model.
- Validate model variant fallback test: make a test request to fallback variant and check for correctness tags in response.

Quick recovery snippets (use carefully):
- Restart agent on node (only if pinned to one machine): sudo systemctl restart redwood-agent && sleep 6 && sudo journalctl -u redwood-agent -n 200 --no-pager | tail -n 40
- Flush local KV cache for route: POST to internal API: curl -X POST "https://internal-api.redwood/cache/flush" -d '{\n  "route": "chat/production",\n  "scope": "local"\n}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN"
- Scale down problematic replica: kubectl -n inference scale deployment recon-prod --replicas=0 && then scale to healthy count after 30s. (DO NOT scale ded-prod; use autoscaler)

Escalation matrix (when to page):
- Page oncall-sre if: P99 latency > 2s for 10+ min, or error rate > 5% for 15+ min.
- Page oncall-eng if: model-serving binary segfaults on multiple nodes or there are cryptic kernel OOMs.
- Page infra-team lead (Evelyn Chu) for cross-region networking failures or consistent node disk pressure.
- Pager: #oncall-sre (PagerDuty) -> email oncall-rotation@redwood.com -> escalate to EM if not acked in 10m.

Known flaky items (notes to self):
- local-redis on control plane sometimes reports high CPU after rolling updates (temp mitigation: restart redis pod after verifying no active migrations).
- grpc-connect-timeout spike around 03:00 UTC occasionally tied to backup window in eu-west. Keep an eye on cron-backup logs.
- Batching headroom config sometimes underestimates for long-seq requests (TODO: add a gauge metric for avg sequence length).

Mini-postmortem template (for quick writeups):
- Incident title:
- Window when first observed:
- Symptoms & alert panels triggered:
- Immediate mitigations performed:
- Root cause hypothesis:
- Follow-ups / owners / jira tickets:

Temporary procedures / experimental fixes (label experiments clearly):
- Experiment: 30s KV cache TTL bump for chat-hot keys (patch id: exp/kv-ttl-30s). Rollout: patch to canary 1 node -> monitor 15m -> increase.
- Temp fallback policy: if model X p99 > 1.5s for 10m, route new requests to quantized variant X-q8 with lower throughput but lower lat. Add metric: routed_to_q8_count.

Handover notes to morning shift (what I will do before I leave):
- Run final sweep and leave a short summary in #shift-handoff channel with: alerts active, what I restarted, any experiments running, and open follow-ups with owners and jitter.
- Leave the synthetic-check logs attached to JIRA ticket if any failure seen.

Open questions / TODOs (short):
- Should we automate KV-ttl bump as a transient policy when rascal-queue > 500? (talk to Product/Optimize team).
- Add a small script that runs all 3 health checks and posts results to slack -> place in /ops/bin/ (low pri).
- Validate that the tenant-rate-limiter rules are not dropping requests during Canary bursts.

Recent quick notes (last few shifts):
- 2024-10-14 02:10 UTC: brief latency spike tied to eu backup window, increased retries led to queue pileup — mitigated by rollback of retry-bump (PR #310).
- 2024-10-22 03:45 UTC: agent OOM on rtx-node-07, replaced host, created JIRA OPS-987 (linked above).

Notes-to-self: keep this doc short, snapshot into Confluence if things settle (label: midwatch-runbook). If you inherit midwatch, first thing: make coffee, then run start sweep.

-- end of draft --

(If this proves useful, extract as a light-weight shift template and add commands as small shell helpers in ops repo.)
